title: {Syn} Fast Inverse Square Root Became Programming Folklore
content:
The fast inverse square root routine became famous for approximating 1/sqrt(x) quickly in graphics code. Its bit-level initial guess and Newton step made it memorable.

Modern hardware often has direct support for similar operations, but the example remains a classic lesson in numerical approximation and machine representation.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
